vulnerabilities.type: Unprotected initializer allows takeover of BuilderWallet admin
vulnerabilities.explanation: BuilderWallet uses an external initializer `init(address _builderAdmin)` that has no access control and no one-time guard. Any address can call `init` at any time (including after deployment) to set/overwrite `builderAdmin`. Since `sweep()` only checks `msg.sender == builderAdmin`, an attacker can first set themselves as `builderAdmin` and then sweep all ERC20 tokens held by the wallet. These wallets are used as deterministic fee recipients via `RiskEngine._computeBuilderWallet()`, so any accrued builder fees sent to the wallet can be stolen permissionlessly.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario:
1) Observe a BuilderWallet address being used as fee recipient (from builderCode) and/or track BuilderFactory.deployBuilder events.
2) After the wallet is deployed, call `BuilderWallet(wallet).init(attackerEOA)` to overwrite `builderAdmin`.
3) Call `BuilderWallet(wallet).sweep(token, attackerEOA)` for each token balance to steal all fees held by the wallet.
4) Repeat whenever new fees accrue, keeping control by re-calling `init` if needed.

prediction.overall_explanation: RiskEngine is largely a stateless math/oracle/risk calculator; most functions are view/pure and don’t directly custody funds. The main concrete, permissionless fund-loss issue is in the BuilderWallet subsystem: its unprotected `init` lets anyone take over `builderAdmin` and drain tokens via `sweep`, which breaks the intended fee-recipient security model and enables theft of builder-fee balances.
